CCLVI. entries.english:
1468, 4 July. Neuhans. — The same man authorizes the same person to absolve the Hohenfurt monastery brothers from their sins and from the ecclesiastical censures imposed on them because of their adherence to the lord of Rosenberg and King George Poděbrad.

CCLVI. Helias, canon and administrator of Litomyšl, specially appointed by the Apostolic See, acolyte of our most holy lord the pope, and parish priest of the parish church of the Blessed and Immaculate Virgin Mary at Neuhans, sends greetings in the Lord to the honorable man Lord Friedrich, a brother of the Altovad monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the diocese of Prague, and wishes him due diligence in the matters entrusted to him. Because of the dangers of the roads, the brothers of your Altovad monastery cannot come to us in person so that provision may be made for their salvation. Nevertheless, by letters of the reverend father, the lord abbot, and the convent of the said monastery, they earnestly sought absolution for the matters entrusted to them and humbly begged us kindly to provide for the salvation of their souls, to absolve them from the ecclesiastical censures incurred by their failure to observe the interdict, and likewise to dispense them from the irregularity they contracted on that account. They have voluntarily bound themselves to contribute to the general treasury against the most perfidious heretics, the cruel enemies of God and his holy Church.

We, therefore, moved by their prayers and acting by the authority of the reverend father in Christ, the lord Lord Rudolf, Bishop of Lavant, legate sent by the Apostolic See with the power of a legate a latere in Bohemia and Poland, for this occasion alone entrust our powers to you, the aforesaid Lord Friedrich, and by these presents delegate to you the authority granted to us, with power to subdelegate. Thus you may absolve all the brothers of the said Altovad monastery who are presently there, except the lord abbot, from all the aforesaid censures by virtue of their contribution, according to the form given to us, and likewise dispense them from the irregularity they contracted on this account, as we ourselves dispense them by these presents in God's name, restoring them to the sacraments of Holy Mother Church and to communion with the faithful. You shall first receive from each of them, except the prior, the solemn surety of an oath in the form of the Church, as the order of the sacred canons directs and requires, that they will henceforth forever obey the commands of the Apostolic See and the Church; and you shall impose salutary penance according to the degree of guilt. Your conscience is charged with all these matters.

In testimony of all this, our seal is attached to these presents. Given at Neuhans in the year of our Lord 1468, on the fourth day of July, in the third year of the pontificate of our most holy father in Christ, our lord Lord Paul II, pope by divine providence. At the lower edge: “h. visa.” The seal is missing.
